claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, I need to gather some information about you and your child/children. Let me begin with a few questions.

**First, could you tell me the name(s) of the child or children you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm helping you with your son **Alex**.

Before I can assess eligibility, I need to understand your circumstances better. Let me start with some key questions.

**How old is Alex, or what is his date of birth?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex is 6 years old.

**Next, does Alex live with you permanently, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for confirming that Alex lives with you.

Now I need to check some important eligibility criteria. Let me read the official guidance to ensure I ask you the right questions.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I've reviewed the eligibility criteria. Now I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. That's an important criterion met.

Now, I need to check your residency and right to reside status, as this can affect eligibility.

**What is your nationality or immigration status? For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or do you have another type of visa or right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. As a British citizen living in the UK, you meet the residency requirements.

Now I have one more important question to confirm your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and maintenance? In other words, do you provide for his needs such as food, clothing, and other living expenses?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I provide for all of Alex's needs - his food, clothing, and everything he needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key criteria:

✓ Alex is under 16 years old (he's 6)
✓ Alex lives with you
✓ You are responsible for Alex and provide for his care and maintenance
✓ You live in the UK
✓ You are a British citizen

Based on the UK government's Child Benefit eligibility rules, you meet all the necessary criteria.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

You meet all the requirements:
- Alex is under 16 years old
- He lives with you
- You are responsible for his care and maintenance
- You are a British citizen living in the UK

You can now proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other children you'd like me to assess, I'm happy to help with those as well.
